      - @19.66s, 23% down: "To understand how the previous node works, / it's important to understand the model of the render / graph of ossia score. / Some environments work in a "push" mode: / nodes generate a texture at a given size, and subsequent / nodes fetch that texture as input. / ossia score works with multiple texture inputs on the same / inlet, to allow multiple separate render passes on the same / depth (Z) buffer: think of each node flowing into a texture inlet / as a separate draw call of the same render pass. / This means that there cannot be a canonical texture input size: / two completely different objects could render to the same port. / Thus, score works in the other direction: inlets (render targets) / have a fixed size. Outlets render in whatever the inlet size of a / following node is. / This means that a single node can render at multiple resolutions: / this allows for shaders that rely on pixel-perfect resolution such as / dithering, etc. to work correctly in all situations. / By default, the inlets will follow the resolution of the closest inlet in the / chain they are connected to, recursively. / If no inlet set an explicit size, it will then be the final render size / output resolution. / Given a chain A -> B -> C -> D -> Window, / if Window renders at 1280x720 and C's input is set at 640x480, then: / - A will render into B at 640x480, / -B will render into C at 640x480, / - C will render into D at 1280x720, / - D will render into Window at 1280x720 / Thus, to set a proper fit mode, one must first set the expected / input resolution in the port: otherwise the render to the render / target will be stretched to fill it and the node will have no effect."

// Everything is computed in output pixels: the image of size texSize is
// scaled to dispSize, then placed so that `alignment` of the leftover
// space (or of the overflow, when cropping) is on each side.
// With alignment = center this matches score's ScaleMode:
//   Original  -> "Original Size"
//   BlackBars -> "Fit (Letterbox)"
//   Fill      -> "Fill (Crop)"
//   Stretch   -> "Stretch"

void main() {
    vec2 renderSize = RENDERSIZE;
    vec2 texSize = IMG_SIZE(inputImage);

    if (texSize.x <= 0.0 || texSize.y <= 0.0) {
        gl_FragColor = bgColor;
        return;
    }

    // Per-axis scale factors that make the image match the output
    vec2 ratio = renderSize / texSize;
